subject: Short-window reserve request for concurrency proof — VelocityAI POC
messages:
From: Caroline Park <caroline@velocity.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick ask — short overnight reserve for concurrency proof

Hi Mateo,

We want to run a short, aggressive concurrency sweep against the Redwood endpoint as part of our acceptance criteria for the VelocityAI integration. The test will be overnight (US Pacific) and is intended to validate p95 tail latency under sustained 400 rps for a 4–6 hour window.

Details:
- Window: Oct 6, 00:00–06:00 PT (approx)
- Target sustained: 400 requests/sec, average prompt length ~80 tokens
- Goal: p95 < 200ms and <2% timeouts
- Failure mode: we’ll need a fallback to a lower-capacity model if we hit throttles, but we want the live environment to show baseline behavior

Can Redwood provide a short-window reserve/credit top-up for this run (we estimate ~90k tokens / 6h), and also confirm whether autoscaling will be allowed to burst above trial caps for the window? We’re on the trial but nearing the limit.

Attached is our quick run plan (velocity_poc_plan.csv) with ramp schedule and expected ramp steps.

Thanks — appreciate a quick turnaround so we can finalize scheduling with the ops team.

—Caroline
Caroline Park
Head of Integrations, VelocityAI
caroline@velocity.ai
+1 (415) 555‑0198

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Caroline Park <caroline@velocity.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Oct 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick ask — short overnight reserve for concurrency proof

Hi Caroline — thanks for the plan and the attachment. We can usually support short-window bursts, but I need to confirm a couple of operational details before I lock in a top-up:

1) Are you able to accept a temporary canary fallback policy (we’ll route to a slightly lower-memory quantized variant if we hit capacity triggers)?
2) Please confirm whether rate limits are global or per‑API key for the test keys you plan to use (your ops note shows a single shared key).
3) We’ll need the exact ramp schedule in the CSV in the hh:mm:seconds format — I see ramp steps but not exact timestamps.

Estimate we should budget for ~120k tokens to be safe (given retries and longer responses). If that works I’ll open a short-window reserve request with Sales Ops and loop in LAURA for approval. Assuming approval, we’ll provision a promoted quota and remove it after the window.

I’ve attached a quick checklist for what we’ll toggle on our end (autoscale burst flag, canary fallback). Can you confirm acceptance of the fallback?

On my side: I’ll coordinate with Ben for the quota authorization.

—Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Oct 2027 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary reserve for VelocityAI POC (short window, overnight)

Team — quick ask: VelocityAI (DEAL-8341) needs a 6‑hour overnight reserve to validate p95 under a 400 rps sustained concurrency sweep. Customer-supplied run plan is attached.

What I’m requesting here:
- Provision a 6‑hour promoted quota for the VelocityAPI key covering up to 150k tokens (safety buffer for retries).
- Enable autoscale burst for the window and allow the canary fallback routing we discussed (quantized variant) if capacity trigger hits.
- Add a short retention flag so we can revert quotas immediately after the window ends.

Why: This is the last acceptance check before they sign. Passing the run significantly de‑risks the deployment (and speeds up contract execution).

Risk notes:
- Run is scheduled outside business hours (low overlap).
- Pushback risk: quota misuse — we’ll require Velocity to confirm exact key and ramp schedule 24h prior; we can revoke if they deviate.

Approvals needed: finance/sales ops signoff for the temporary promotional credit. Ben — can you confirm we can cover this under the trial top-up buffer or whether we need a small promo credit issuance? Laura — can you approve a one-off promoted quota and flag the billing record so this run doesn’t auto-bill?

Thanks — I’m available on Slack if easier.

—Mateo
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 6 Oct 2027 15:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary reserve for VelocityAI POC (short window, overnight)

Mateo / Ben — approved.

Decision: Approve a short-window promoted quota of 150k tokens for VelocityAI for the window Oct 6 00:00–06:00 PT. Conditions:
- Provision as a temporary promo credit (non-billable) and set automatic revoke at 06:05 PT.
- Require Velocity to publish the exact API key and timestamped ramp schedule by Oct 5 16:00 PT; we’ll gate provisioning until we have that.
- Enable autoscale burst and the canary fallback route; set a telemetry alert to paging if p95 exceeds 500ms for more than 5 consecutive minutes.

I’ve created a quick Ops ticket and attached the run plan to the ticket. See ticket: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/8341 (linked) and I’ve included a small note on the billing record to mark this as promotional.

Ben — please push the promo credit now and confirm when the quota is visible on their dashboard so I can notify the customer. Mateo — once Velocity confirms the key/schedule, greenlight the run.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
